unit.sep: Identify corresponding quantities,construct from a centre,derive scale relationships and audit model assumptions.
unit.careers: Illustrative design,photography,packaging and model making;no professional engineering/capacity certification.
unit.focus: Positive linear factors,including fractional reductions,and their square/cube area/volume relationships. Negative factors are excluded by the source.
unit.phenomenon: A fictional designer doubles a container's lengths but predicts only twice the capacity,while a photo resized in one direction loses its shape.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Corresponding sides,rays from a centre,unit-square/layer models,container nets and locked-aspect digital resizing.
unit.drivingQuestion: Which quantities really stay proportional when a model changes size? KICD: How is similarity and enlargement applied in real life?
unit.storylineThread: Similarity → centre → positive enlarge/shrink → non-origin centre → area → volume → inverse ratios → applications → net plan → construction → digital audit → independent evidence.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Digital literacy: The learner develops the skills of connecting and interacting with digital technology when using digital resources to learn more on the use and application of similarity and enlargement.
Creativity and Imagination: the learner acquires networking skills when drawing images of given objects under a particular enlargement scale factor.
unit.values: Responsibility: The learner takes care of objects collected from the immediate environment.
unit.pcis: Environment and technology: the learner acquires the skill of sorting in managing the environment after collecting and sorting the objects and containers.
unit.content: Similarity between objects; Enlargement Scale Factors (Linear, Area and Volume) (Negative scale factor will not be included); Application of Similarity and Enlargement

sections.title: 1. Establish similarity
sections.prompt: Decide which of QandRare similar to photoPusing the given corresponding width/height ratios and angles. State two defining properties of similar figures and explain why equal right angles alone cannot establish rectangle similarity.
sections.exemplar: P/Qratios6/3=8/4=2,allrightangles,so similar. P/Rratios6/3=2and7/4=1.75differ,so not similar. Corresponding angles agree and corresponding side lengths have a common ratio;rectangles can all have right angles yet different aspect ratios.

sections.title: 2. Centre and positive-factor construction
sections.prompt: Plot the SE12 triangles,extend corresponding rays and determine centreEandpositivek,checking more than one pair. Construct D'under that same transformation. Separately construct the image ofDfork=1/2aboutE. Show centre-to-point checks and explain why simply multiplying D's coordinates bykuses an unstated origin.
sections.exemplar: Consistent rays meetE(1,1);side ratios4/2=2and2/1=2givek2. D'=E+2(D−E)=(5,7);halfimageE+(D−E)/2=(2,2.5). Both lie on rayEDat corresponding distance ratios. Multiplying coordinates directly assumes centreO,which differs fromE.

sections.title: 3. Linear,area and volume factors
sections.prompt: Find the triangle original/image areas and their ratio from the coordinate data. For the containerfind volume factor,image volume and area factor. For the separate half-scale figurefind image area. Explain why the factors are k,k²,k³,and why an area/volume ratio alone cannot prove two unverified objects similar.
sections.exemplar: Trianglebase2,height1,area1cm²;imagebase4,height2,area4cm²,ratio4. Containerk2givesvolume8andimage96cm³;area factor4. Half-scalefigurearea40×(1/2)²=10cm². Products of one,two or three corresponding scaled dimensions give the exponents. Equal area/volume alone does not establish corresponding angles/common length ratios.

sections.title: 4. Practical use and limits
sections.prompt: Give one concrete use of similarity/enlargement supported by a result above. Explain one limitation in treating an ideal container volume as its verified usable capacity. Name an actual observation/artifact a teacher would need to confirm construction or digital documentation skill.
